 Order
07.12.2023
01.
This writ petition came to be filed on 04.04.2012.

At the time of filing of the writ petition, the petitioners claim to be in knowledge of section 4 notification dated 07.08.2010 issued under the J&K Land Acquisition Act, Svt. 1990 whereby acquisition of land falling in khasra numbers as mentioned in the said notification was declared.

In the said khasra numbers, the petitioners claimed to be in use and occupation of the land comprised in khasra numbers 1795/1660 min (03 marlas),
1795/1660 min (19 marlas) and 1794/1660 (14 marlas), the purpose for which the acquisition was intended for construction of PWD Dak-Banglow at village Korya, Patwar Halqua Feller, Kishtwar.
02.

However, the fact remains that at the time of filing of the writ petition, the land acquisition exercise set into effect had culminated in passing of a final award dated 04.03.2011 vide which the khasra numbers above mentioned relatable to the petitioners also stood declared to be acquired.

1 03.

Learned counsel for the petitioners submits that despite this final acquisition award, the possession of the petitioners qua khasra no. 1794/1660 (14 Marlas) continued to be with the petitioners whereat they have their residential house and it t is only 03 marlas of land in khasra no.
1795/1660 min (03 marlas) which came to be used for the passage to and fro from the Dak-Banglow and that the construction of the Dak-Banglow has taken place with respect to the rest of the khasra numbers which too came under the acquisition.
04.

Learned counsel for the petitioners submits that the present position of the available two khasra numbers i.e. 1795/1660 min (19 marlas) and 1794/1660 (14 marlas) as on date is still with the petitioners and that there is a residential constructed house obtaining at the site in which the petitioners along with their family members are residing and that the site of said construction house though falling in the khasra numbers stated to have been acquired is no more required for the of Dak- Banglow.
05. Let the petitioners place on record the photographs of the residential house as is claimed to be existing at the site of the available two khasra numbers.
Let the needful be done within a period of two weeks.

06. In addition, the learned counsel for the petitioners is also directed to place on record the revenue report generated pursuant to the petitioners' application submitted for seeking de-notification of the land in the said two kharas numbers 1795/1660 min (19 marlas) and 1794/1660 (14 marlas) before the next date of hearing.

07. In the meantime, Mr. Ravinder Gupta, learned AAG appearing on behalf of the respondent nos.
2 & 4 is directed to seek instructions from the PWD Department as to whether the Dak- Banglow premises requires the entire land which became the subject-matter of acquisition award or that the present premises of the Dak-Banglow suffices the purpose.

08. Mr. Kaushal Parihar, learned counsel for the petitioners is also directed to apprise this Court as to whether the compensation awarded with respect to the aforesaid two khasra numbers has been withdrawn by the recorded owners/the petitioners or not.
09. List this case on 27.12.2023.
(RAHUL BHARTI) JUDGE JAMMU 07.12.2023 Muneesh Ghulam Mohd.
